identity.title: Grand-design Spiral Arms in a Young Forming Circumstellar Disk

paper_type_evidence.quote: We then perform synthetic observations and compare our model with a recent high-resolution observation of a young stellar object Elias 2-27, whose circumstellar disk has grand design spiral arms.

question.value: Can recurrent gravitational-instability material spiral arms in a long-term resistive MHD disk-formation simulation explain the grand-design spiral arms of Elias 2-27 seen by ALMA?

evidence.quote: Our model suggests that the grand design spiral arms around Elias 2-27 are consistent with material arms formed by gravitational instability.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00498.S.

continuum_bandwidth.value: 6.8 GHz (simulated, chosen close to the Elias 2-27 observation)

evidence.quote: We chose observation parameters as close to (cite: e2-27) as possible; the bandwidth is 6.8 GHz, the integration time is 12.5 minutes
We use “alma.cycle4.5.cfg" array configuration file
This produces a synthetic beam of $0.29\, {\rm arcsec} \times 0.26\, {\rm arcsec}$, which is very close to the original observation.
the integration time is 12.5 minutes

what.value: Observed ALMA 1.3 mm continuum image of Elias 2-27 and its disk parameters (disk mass ~0.14 Msun, surface density estimates)

evidence.quote: Observations of Elias 2-27 suggest that its disk can be indeed massive, $M_{\rm disk}\sim 0.14\, {\rm M_\odot}$ (cite: andrews09; e2-27).

what.value: Accretion rate 8e-8 Msun/yr and spectral type M0 of Elias 2-27

evidence.quote: we adopt $\dot{M}=8 \times 10^{-8}\, {\rm M_\odot\, yr^{-1}}$ to calculate the accretion luminosity based on the observation of Elias 2-27 (cite: najita15)

what.value: Dust opacity tables, composite aggregate model, normal abundance

evidence.quote: we adopt the monochromatic opacity tables of (cite: semenov) [^2], using the composite aggregate dust model of the normal abundance.

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: 3D nested-grid resistive MHD simulation of collapsing 1.25 Msun Bonnor-Ebert-like core with Ohmic dissipation and barotropic EOS, run to ~47,000 yr protostar age

evidence.quote: at the end of the simulation the protostar age reaches about 47,000 years.
we perform simulated observation using the *simobserve* and *simanalyze* tasks
the Briggs waiting with the robustness of 0.5
We refer readers to (cite: mh13) and (cite: machida14; machida16) for the details.
we adopt the barotropic approximation as in (cite: mm12)
We calculate evolution of the central protostar using the STELLAR stellar evolution code (cite: yb08; hosokawa13; sakurai15), as in (cite: mh13).

results_numeric.quantity: Disk radius toward end of Class-I

evidence.quote: Toward the end of the Class-I phase, the disk size becomes larger than 200 AU in the expanding phases with spiral arms.
The disk-to-star mass ratio remains almost constant and is about 30-40% throughout the Class-0 and I phases.
the occurrence probability of the spiral arms is about 50%.

findings_qualitative.value: Spiral arms disappear in a few rotations but re-form recurrently as the disk becomes unstable again

evidence.quote: new spiral arms form recurrently as the disk soon becomes unstable again by gas accretion.

claims.hypothesis: Recurrent GI material spiral arms can form in a young resistive-MHD disk
claims.result: Grand-design m=2 arms form recurrently with Q~1 and persist through Class-0/I
claims.finding: Gravitational torque is a key angular momentum transport process

evidence.quote: Such recurrent spiral arms persist throughout the Class-0 and I phase.

claims.hypothesis: Elias 2-27 spiral arms can be material arms from GI
claims.experiment: Synthetic 1.3 mm ALMA observation of a snapshot compared with observation
claims.result: Disk size, brightness and arm thickness largely consistent; no gaps or outflow reproduced
claims.finding: Observed arms are consistent with GI material arms

evidence.quote: Therefore, we conclude that the observed spiral arms can be well explained by material spiral arms formed by gravitational instability.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Density wave scenario favored by Pérez et al. rejected in favor of recurrent material arms

evidence.quote: While (cite: e2-27) favored the density wave scenario pointing out that material spiral arms should disappear in a few orbital periods

limitations_admitted.value: No ambipolar diffusion, Hall effect or radiation transfer in the MHD run; temperature post-processed

evidence.quote: The current MHD simulation does not consider ambipolar diffusion, the Hall effect and radiation transfer.

limitations_admitted.value: Gap-like structures and absent small-scale outflow not matched

evidence.quote: some features do not match perfectly. For example, gap-like structures exist in Elias 2-27 but we do not find any significant gap in our synthetic observation.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single snapshot chosen to resemble the target; comparison is visual only
Accretion rate and inclination tuned to match observation
Barotropic EOS and fixed opacity (lower than Pérez et al.) affect the Q and brightness

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA data acknowledged by project code; simulation code not stated as public

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Small; only the published Elias 2-27 image is needed for comparison (<~1 GB); main cost is the MHD simulation.
reproducibility.score_reason: Primarily a simulation paper with a custom unreleased MHD code; the ALMA part is a simulated observation with partial settings.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main results come from a non-public simulation and are qualitative comparisons.
